newsitem.title: ITALY: POLL - Italy July CPI seen flat, yr/yr hurt by stats.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Italy July CPI seen flat, yr/yr hurt by stats.

text.p: Italy's monthly consumer price inflation in July should benefit from cuts in electricity, gas and telephone tariffs implemented on July 1 but the yearly rate will rise due to unfavourable statistical comparisons with last year, a Reuters poll showed.
The 13 analysts surveyed on average saw July CPI staying flat monthly and rising 1.6 percent yearly.
In June, CPI inflation also showed no change from the previous month and was 1.4 percent year on year, falling for the fifth consecutive month from 1.6 percent in May.
In July 1996, prices fell 0.2 percent monthly and rose 3.6 percent yearly.
Next Monday and Tuesday, 11 sample Italian cities publish their preliminary CPI data for July and national statistics body ISTAT will announce the final figure on August 5.

Analysts agreed that in July the monthly figure will be more important than the yearly rate because CPI for the same month in 1996 was extremely positive making a drop in the yearly rate difficult. They saw the reduction in tariffs having an effect of between 0.05 and 0.1 percent on the monthly rate.
"The only uncertainty this month arises from the quarterly rent reviews," said Rodolfo Dozio, analyst at Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI).

Lucia Trevisan, economist at brokers Caboto said, "This could lead to a positive monthly variation but I don't think rents were substantial this quarter because rent hikes are linked to CPI which has fallen sharply over the past months."
Trevisan added that another factor which could help contain inflation this month was the extension of fare discounts by national airline carrier Alitalia.
